articles.title: Itália multa Meta em R$ 5 bilhões por acessar fotos e vídeos de usuários sem consentimento | G1
articles.standfirst: Autoridade italiana acusa empresa de acessar imagens de usuários de celulares Android sem informá-los ou obter autorização.
articles.summary: Autoridade italiana acusa empresa de acessar imagens de usuários de celulares Android sem informá-los ou obter autorização.
articles.body:
Justiça de São Paulo proíbe Meta de usar conteúdo jornalístico sem autorização — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

A autoridade de proteção de dados da Itália multou a Meta em € 805 milhões (R$ 5 bilhões) neste sábado (14), sob a acusação de que a empresa acessou fotos e vídeos de 20 milhões de usuários do sistema Android sem obter consentimento ou informá-los sobre a prática.

A decisão se soma a outras punições aplicadas à dona do Facebook, Instagram e WhatsApp na Europa por problemas relacionados à proteção de dados pessoais.

A punição envolve uma função do aplicativo do Facebook chamada " Obtenha sugestões da galeria enquanto navega no Facebook ", disponível desde 2023 . O recurso sugere fotos e vídeos armazenados na galeria do celular para que o usuário os utilize em publicações na rede social.

Segundo a autoridade italiana, a Meta solicitava uma única autorização para acessar a galeria do aparelho, válida para diferentes funções do aplicativo. Antes da solicitação, porém, apresentava apenas um aviso genérico sobre a ativação de outras funcionalidades, sem esclarecer que a permissão também permitiria o uso das imagens para fazer sugestões de publicações.

Além disso, a função vinha ativada por padrão. Com a autorização concedida, o aplicativo podia ler todo o arquivo de fotos do dispositivo, geralmente de forma permanente. Segundo o órgão, nem o usuário nem a própria autoridade conseguiam verificar quais informações eram efetivamente utilizadas.

A investigação começou em julho de 2025, após uma denúncia do Centro de Defesa dos Consumidores de Bolzano, no norte da Itália, e incluiu uma análise técnica conduzida pela própria autoridade.

O órgão considerou que a prática violou o artigo 122 do Código de Privacidade italiano, que incorpora regras da diretiva europeia ePrivacy. A legislação protege as informações armazenadas nos celulares e exige consentimento livre e informado para qualquer acesso a esses dados, independentemente de haver transmissão das informações ou comprovação de prejuízo ao usuário.

A autoridade também rejeitou o argumento da Meta de que o caso deveria ser analisado pelo regulador irlandês. Segundo o órgão italiano, as regras da diretiva ePrivacy não preveem o mecanismo de atendimento por uma única autoridade nacional, utilizado em outras investigações de proteção de dados na União Europeia.

A decisão determina que a Meta adote mudanças no funcionamento do recurso em até 60 dias . A empresa deverá solicitar uma autorização específica para acessar a galeria, explicar claramente a finalidade da função e informar como desativá-la.

A ferramenta também deverá permanecer desativada por padrão, inclusive para usuários que já tenham concedido a permissão geral de acesso às fotos. Depois do prazo, quem não tiver dado um consentimento válido não poderá ativá-la.

A empresa terá ainda de comunicar à autoridade italiana, em até 30 dias , as iniciativas iniciadas para cumprir a determinação e, em até 90 dias , as medidas efetivamente adotadas.

A investigação envolveu cerca de 20 milhões de usuários de Android na Itália. Para definir o valor da multa, o órgão considerou o número de pessoas afetadas, a duração da irregularidade — que ainda continuava para usuários que não atualizaram o aplicativo ou já haviam concedido a autorização —, um precedente contra a empresa em 2019 e a colaboração considerada insuficiente durante a investigação.

A autoridade reconheceu como atenuante as mudanças implementadas pela Meta depois da denúncia, mas avaliou que elas foram tardias e limitadas aos usuários que atualizaram o aplicativo. O valor da multa equivale a aproximadamente 0,47% do faturamento mundial do grupo.

O procedimento não investigou se as fotos e os vídeos foram utilizados para treinar sistemas de inteligência artificial, prática que a Meta nega. A autoridade italiana informou que poderá realizar uma investigação separada sobre uma nova função, lançada em 2026, que permite processar na nuvem os conteúdos da galeria do celular.

As preocupações com a privacidade também chegaram aos óculos inteligentes da Meta.

Em março de 2026, uma reportagem de jornais suecos revelou que funcionários terceirizados responsáveis por analisar imagens dos dispositivos Ray-Ban Meta para treinar a inteligência artificial da empresa tinham acesso a registros de pessoas em situações íntimas , como no banheiro, trocando de roupa e durante relações sexuais.

O caso levou à abertura de um processo em um tribunal da Califórnia, nos Estados Unidos . A ação acusa a Meta de propaganda enganosa e de desrespeitar leis de privacidade. A empresa afirma que o processamento das imagens segue seus termos de serviço e que os registros são borrados antes da revisão humana para proteger a identidade das pessoas.

Em dezembro de 2024, a Comissão Irlandesa de Proteção de Dados (DPC), principal órgão regulador de privacidade da União Europeia (UE), multou a empresa em € 251 milhões (R$ 1,5 bilhão) por uma falha de segurança no Facebook que expôs informações de 29 milhões de contas em todo o mundo.

Na ocasião, a Meta afirmou que recorreria da decisão e declarou ter uma ampla gama de medidas para proteger os usuários de suas plataformas. A falha havia sido comunicada pela própria empresa à DPC em 2018, depois que hackers exploraram uma vulnerabilidade no recurso "Exibir como", que permite visualizar como um perfil aparece para outras pessoas.

Entre as informações expostas estavam nomes completos , contatos , localização , local de trabalho , datas de nascimento e dados pessoais de filhos dos usuários .

Em novembro de 2022, a empresa também recebeu uma multa de € 265 milhões (R$ 1,6 bilhão) do regulador irlandês, após uma investigação sobre a exposição de dados de mais de 530 milhões de usuários do Facebook . O vazamento, identificado em 2019, envolveu a coleta automatizada de informações de perfis por meio de um método conhecido como scraping.

articles.title: Himachal woman buys second-hand iPhone 12 for Rs 29,000 from Chandigarh shop, handset stops working within 4 days despite six-month warranty, seller takes it back promising repair or refund but fails to do either, consumer commission orders Rs 59,000 payout with interest
articles.summary: UNA: A district consumer disputes redressal commission in Himachal Pradesh's Una has directed a Chandigarh-based mobile shop to refund Rs 29,000 to a
articles.body: UNA: A district consumer disputes redressal commission in Himachal Pradesh's Una has directed a Chandigarh-based mobile shop to refund Rs 29,000 to a woman who purchased a second-hand iPhone 12 that stopped working within four days of purchase.The commission also ordered the shop to pay 9% annual interest on the amount from the date the consumer complaint was filed until realisation. It further awarded Rs 20,000 as compensation for mental harassment and Rs 10,000 towards litigation expenses.In its November 2, 2026, order, the commission observed that the shop had sold a defective handset despite providing a six-month warranty and subsequently failed to repair it or refund the purchase amount.According to the complaint, Mamta Kadyan, a resident of Rakkar Colony in Una, purchased a second-hand blue iPhone 12 from Arohi Mobile Hub, located in Sector 22B, Chandigarh, on October 27, 2023. She paid Rs 29,000 for the handset, for which the shop issued invoice number 159. The invoice carried a handwritten assurance of a six-month warranty in case the phone developed any problem.However, the handset stopped working within three to four days. Kadyan informed the shop about the problem and visited its premises on November 3, 2023, following which the shop took the phone back, promising to get it checked and repaired through an authorised person.The shop allegedly assured her that if the problem could not be resolved, it would refund the entire Rs 29,000 within 15 days. It also obtained the QR code and bank account details of her husband to facilitate the payment.However, despite repeated telephone calls by Kadyan and her husband, neither a functional handset nor a refund was provided. The shop allegedly refused to return a working phone or pay back the money on January 18, 2024.The consumer subsequently sent a legal notice to the shop, but it did not respond.During the proceedings, the complainant submitted her affidavit, purchase invoice and a copy of the legal notice as evidence. The commission noted that the invoice established the purchase price and the six-month warranty, while the legal notice showed that the shop had been informed of her grievance.The commission also noted that the shop had been duly served but did not appear before it or file a reply. It was consequently proceeded against ex parte.Holding that the evidence established that the shop had sold a defective phone and failed to honour its warranty obligations, the commission ruled that there was deficiency in service.The order was passed by commission president D R Thakur and member Anoop Kumar. The shop has been directed to make the payments within 30 days of receiving a copy of the order.Stay updated with the latest Dehradun news. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: Tesla is inviting some people to buy a Cybercab ‘for personal use’ — but read the fine print
articles.summary: Tesla is selling the $29,990 Cybercab for personal use, but a mandatory $299/month fee, Austin-only geofences, and an active NHTSA audit raise big questions.
articles.body: Tesla is doubling, or perhaps tripling down on its bold claims of an autonomous future with the offer to “select customers” to purchase a Cybercab for “personal use.” But the gilded, steering-wheel-free two-seater will “only be available in supported service areas” — meaning you’ll only be able to buy one if you live in one of the cities where Tesla currently operates its Robotaxi service. The price of a Cybercab is listed at $29,990, plus a mandatory $299-a-month “Autonomy Subscription.” Tesla’s Robotaxi account on X announced the new offer, including screenshots of the order page and the invite email. But don’t expect a fleet of personally owned Cybercabs to suddenly materialize on public roads: “Initial availability is limited,” the invitation email warns. [Image: [Image: [Image: Tesla began offering rides in the Cybercab as part of its Model Y-powered Robotaxi service in Austin in September. The company now has 278 Cybercabs in operation, representing approximately 40 percent of its fleet, according to the crowd-sourced Robotaxi Tracker. The inclusion of a mandatory $299/month subscription is sure to rankle some fans who may have dreamed of cruising around in a $30,000 driverless Tesla, as originally promised by Tesla CEO Elon Musk when he first introduced the Cybercab in 2024. Musk made no mention of the Autonomy Subscription at that event, though it shouldn’t come as too much of a surprise given the $99/month fee Tesla currently charges for its Full Self-Driving (FSD) feature. Still, that money adds up over time. Over a standard 5-year ownership period, the mandatory $299/month fee adds $17,940 to the sticker price (even with the first month included), bringing the real baseline cost to roughly $47,600 before taxes, charging, and insurance — more than a brand-new Model 3 or Model Y that you can actually drive anywhere in the country. Unlike a standard Tesla where canceling FSD just reverts the car to manual driving, canceling the $299/month Autonomy Subscription renders the Cybercab completely unusable on public roads because there is no manual fallback. In effect, the car becomes a brick. Additionally, Tesla says that buyers will have to put down a $1,000 non-refundable deposit just to get in line for a December delivery window that isn’t guaranteed. One of the biggest selling points of Musk’s 2024 “We, Robot” pitch was that regular people could buy a Cybercab and add it to Tesla’s Robotaxi network to earn passive income while they sleep or work. But the order terms explicitly prohibit owners from using the vehicle for commercial purposes — meaning no Uber, no DoorDash, and no putting it on Tesla’s own Robotaxi network to offset the $299/month fee. Tesla AI chief Ashok Elluswamy has floated Q2 2027 as a possible target for letting customer cars join the network, so early buyers are paying full freight with zero way to monetize the car. Of course, that’s just the fine print. On X, Tesla CEO Elon Musk was promising a much wider rollout, subject — of course — to “regulatory approval.” Musk frequently frames regulatory approval as the primary external bottleneck holding back his robotaxi timelines as a way to shift focus away from Tesla’s technological shortcomings. (For what it’s worth, he also called his own company’s $299/month Autonomy Subscription “too high,” arguing that it should actually be $115/month or closer to Tesla’s $99/month Full Self-Driving subscription.) But Musk seemed more focused on taunting YouTuber Marques Brownlee, who promised to shave his head if Tesla delivered a Cybercab for under $30,000 before 2027, than answering any of the litany of safety and liability questions raised by this offer. (For his part, Brownlee says he thinks his hair is safe.) For starters, how does Tesla plan on selling a vehicle that doesn’t comply with current Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards that require traditional controls like steering wheels and pedals? Tesla says the Autonomy Subscription covers autonomous driving, maintenance, and towing, but explicitly excludes auto insurance. The company hasn’t explained how personal auto insurers will underwrite a car with no human driver, or how liability is split between the owner and Tesla if the vehicle causes an accident while operating autonomously. Nor has Tesla disclosed how it selects invited buyers or how many units are earmarked for private sale versus its internal fleet. Then there is the small matter of the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration already opening a formal audit into how Tesla self-certified a vehicle without a steering wheel, pedals, or side mirrors. Tesla submitted its legal justification to NHTSA in October, requested that the entire response be kept confidential, and is now taking customer deposits while NHTSA’s ruling is still pending. Which means early buyers aren’t just paying $47,600 for a geofenced car they aren’t allowed to drive — they’re putting down non-refundable cash on a vehicle the federal government hasn’t even decided is street-legal.

articles.title: American Pickers star Frank Fritz’s $6 million estate dispute heads to trial November 16; father challenges 2023 will, claiming stroke left him unable to make legal decisions as friends defend his final wishes
articles.summary: More than two years after ‘American Pickers’ star Frank Fritz died at the age of 60, a bitter legal battle over his estate is heading to trial.
articles.body: More than two years after ‘American Pickers’ star Frank Fritz died at the age of 60, a bitter legal battle over his estate is heading to trial. The probate hearing is scheduled to begin on November 16 in Scott County, Iowa, with Fritz’s biological father, Bill, challenging a will that names some of the reality TV star’s close friends as beneficiaries.The dispute has continued despite multiple mediation sessions, which failed to produce an agreement. Annette Oberlander Willows, one of Fritz’s close friends and a beneficiary named in the contested will, said the matter will now be left to the court unless the two sides reach a settlement before the trial.“I’m feeling very confident about the trial,” Oberlander said, according to The Des Moines Register, declining to discuss the specifics of the case because of the ongoing legal proceedings. “I’m very confident that Frank’s last wishes will be upheld in the court of law.”The value of Fritz’s estate has been estimated at nearly $6 million, although no official figure is available. An Iowa judge has sealed the probate case, including the will, leaving details of his assets and other filings inaccessible to the public.Why Frank Fritz’s father is challenging his willAt the centre of the dispute is the question of whether Fritz was mentally capable of understanding and signing a will in 2023, following a debilitating stroke. His father’s legal team is questioning the validity of the document, while his friends believe it reflects his final wishes.The issue dates back to July 2022, when Fritz was found unresponsive on the floor of his Davenport home. Doctors later determined that he had suffered a stroke. His recovery was difficult, with subsequent hospitalisations for seizures, high blood pressure and pneumonia-like symptoms, according to 911 recordings published by The Sun.In August 2022, a petition for emergency guardianship was filed, stating that a guardian was necessary to prevent immediate harm to Fritz.“Because of his stroke, Mr. Fritz’s decision-making capacity is so impaired that he is unable to care for his own safety, or to provide for necessities such as food, shelter, clothing or medical care,” the petition stated.It also claimed that he was “unable to make, communicate or carry out important decisions concerning his own financial affairs”.A judge granted the guardianship, citing a letter from Fritz’s doctor indicating that he was unable to make decisions for himself. Several documents in the case, including the doctor’s letter, remain sealed. However, a public care plan filed a few weeks later indicated that Fritz did not have a living will at the time.By the time of his guardian’s final report following his death, Fritz was listed as having a will. The document was reportedly prepared in 2023, around eight months after the guardianship was established.Father’s lawyer says court’s earlier finding could invalidate the willBill Fritz’s lawyer, Cory Gourley, has previously argued that the judge’s finding that Fritz “does not have the capacity to execute any legal documents on his own behalf” is crucial evidence that the 2023 will should be set aside.Friends, however, have maintained that Fritz recovered and was in control of his faculties and thoughts during the period before his death. They previously told the Des Moines Register, part of the USA TODAY Network, that he was well enough to reconnect with his former co-star and friend Mike Wolfe after three years apart. He also reportedly enjoyed a night out with friends shortly before the holidays.If the will is declared invalid, Fritz’s estate would be distributed according to the legal hierarchy of blood relatives. As an only child who was unmarried and had no children, his father would almost certainly inherit the assets.Friends and father offer different accounts of Frank Fritz’s personal lifeThe legal dispute has also brought conflicting accounts of Fritz’s relationship with his father and the people closest to him into focus.Gourley has described Bill and Frank as having a close relationship, saying they went on vacations together and regularly visited each other, with Bill travelling to Iowa and Frank visiting Texas. He also claimed that when the guardianship was put in place, the defendants “cut off all access to Frank”.Oberlander, meanwhile, has described Fritz as someone whose life was surrounded by close friendships. She said acquaintances in the Quad Cities area stepped in to care for him after his stroke.According to her, apart from his mother, who died in 2013, Fritz did not have consistent or strong relationships with members of his biological family. Court documents filed in the guardianship case also stated that he had “no living relatives he maintains contact with”.Frank Fritz’s journey to fame with ‘American Pickers’Fritz rose to fame alongside Mike Wolfe when their antique-hunting series ‘American Pickers’ premiered on the History Channel in 2010. Known for his dark beard, quick smile and passion for vintage motorcycles, he became a familiar face to viewers.The show followed Wolfe and Fritz as they travelled across the country, exploring backroads and small-town streets in search of antiques, collectibles and stories behind the objects they discovered. Their easygoing chemistry and shared enthusiasm helped turn the series into a popular reality television hit.Wolfe paid tribute to his friend in an Instagram post shortly after his death, recalling their adventures before the show made them television stars.“Before the show, we would take off together to places we never knew existed with no destination in mind and just the shared passion to discover something interesting and historic,” Wolfe wrote.“Who would have ever dreamed we would share the cockpit of a white cargo van in front of millions of people interested in our adventures.”He also remembered Fritz for his authenticity, writing, “Frank had a way of reaching the hearts of so many by just being himself.”A persistent back injury and debilitating Crohn’s disease eventually forced Fritz to leave the show shortly before the COVID-19 pandemic. He subsequently faced a series of health complications and died in September 2024, aged 60.Frank Fritz’s friends await a final celebration of lifeThe ongoing legal dispute has also delayed the celebration of life that Fritz’s friends want to organise. While they have found personal ways to remember him, they hosted a public tribute in May in Savanna, Illinois, bringing together people who had known him at different stages of his life, including his school years.To mark the second anniversary of his death, Oberlander recently visited the nursing home where Fritz spent many of his final days and reminisced with the staff. She regularly volunteers there, offering haircuts to residents.She later spent the day at home watching some of her favourite episodes of ‘American Pickers’. Oberlander said she missed both Fritz’s larger-than-life personality and the quieter moments they shared, including everyday conversations, lunches and watching television together during his hospital stays.“I want to be able to give him the celebration of life that he desired,” Oberlander said. “I want his friends and fans to be able to celebrate his passing once and for all. That’s what’s most important to me.“I want Frank to be at peace.”Get the latest TV News, TV Shows and more. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Here are our favorite deals from REI’s giant Holiday Sale
articles.summary: REI’s latest seasonal promo is basically an early Black Friday sale on camping gear, with discounts on everything from Garmin watches to satellite communicators.
articles.body: Black Friday has become a shopping season of its own, with retailers once again offering discounts well ahead of the actual shopping holiday. We’ve already rounded up some of the best early Black Friday deals we’ve come across, but if you’re looking to save on outdoor gear or pick up something for an upcoming trip, REI’s annual Holiday Sale, which runs through November 23rd, is worth checking out. As usual, the outdoor retailer is offering discounts on everything from smartwatches to camping equipment. In some cases, we’re seeing some of the lowest prices we’ve seen on our favorite wearables, including Garmin’s Forerunner 570, while gadgets like the InReach Mini 3 are also receiving sizable discounts. REI members can also use promo code HOLIDAY2026 to save 20 percent on one full-price item, plus an additional 20 percent on one REI Outlet item. To save you time, we’ve sifted through the deluge of discounts to find an assortment of deals we recommend here at The Verge. We’ve also noted when competing retailers are offering lower prices on the same items, so you can be sure you’re getting the best deal possible. Featured Products Garmin Forerunner 570 REI Siesta Hooded 20 Sleeping Bag Mpowerd Luci Solar String Lights: Color Exped MegaMat Duo Garmin InReach Mini 3 Plus Kelty Low Loveseat Soundcore Liberty 5 Rumpl Original Puffy Blanket Smartwatches and fitness tech [Product: Garmin Forerunner 570 | [Product: Garmin Venu 4 | * REI, Amazon, and Best Buy are also selling the Garmin Lily 2 Active for $249.99 ($50 off), which is its lowest price to date. The stylish smartwatch is a great budget-friendly Garmin, especially for people with smaller wrists. Like the standard Lily 2, it offers basic fitness tracking, notifications, and up to five days of battery life; however, the so-called “Active” model adds a physical button, built-in GPS, and support for more sports tracking. Read our Lily 2 review. * The Garmin Vivoactive 6 has returned to its all-time low of $249.99 ($50 off) at Amazon, Walmart, and REI. The fitness watch offers up to 11 days of battery life and tracks a range of workouts, including walking, running, cycling, HIIT, golf, and more. It also provides extensive health monitoring, including wrist-based heart rate detection, menstrual cycle and pregnancy tracking, and a customizable morning report that summarizes helpful health-related info. However, it lacks ECG compatibility, though it does have a slightly slimmer profile than its predecessor. [Product: Garmin Fenix 8 | * The Wahoo Kickr V6 Smart Trainer is on sale at REI for $679.99 ($170 off). Like the more affordable Kickr Core 2 we covered in July, the Kickr V6 turns your existing bike into an indoor exercise bike, with Wi-Fi and Bluetooth connectivity for pairing with apps like Zwift. However, the higher-end trainer offers up to 2,200W of resistance and can replicate inclines of up to 20 percent, compared to the Core 2’s 1,800W and 16 percent. It also provides more accurate power measurements and is designed so that indoor rides feel more natural. Phone accessories and entertainment [Product: EcoFlow Rapid Magnetic Power Bank | * If you own an older iPhone with a Lightning port, you can grab InfinityLab’s InstantGo 10,000 Power Bank for $41.93 (about $28 off) at REI. The portable battery features a 10,000mAh capacity and a built-in Lightning cable, making it a solid all-in-one option for days when you won’t be near an outlet. It also supports passthrough charging, so you can charge your phone and the power bank at the same time. * DJI’s Osmo Mobile 8 is on sale for around $128.99 ($21 off) at REI, Amazon, and Best Buy, which is $10 shy of its best price to date. The smartphone gimbal supports 360-degree horizontal rotation and Apple’s DockKit, which allows the gimbal to track and follow pets and people across a wider range of camera apps. This discounted Advanced Tracking Combo also includes a multifunctional module for tracking people and pets, as well as a built-in tripod and extension rod that make it easier to film yourself without someone behind the camera. [Product: Soundcore Liberty 5 | * You can buy Soundcore’s AeroFit 2 for $79.99 ($20 off) at REI, Amazon, and Best Buy, which is $2 shy of their lowest price to date. Their open-ear design lets you listen to music while staying vigilant in your surroundings; they also feature adjustable ear hooks for a secure fit, IP55 water and dust resistance, and up to 42 hours of battery life with the included charging case. [Product: Anker Nebula P1 projector | Communication and safety gear [Product: Garmin InReach Mini 3 Plus | * Garmin’s base InReach Mini 3 is available from REI, Amazon, and Garmin for around $349 ($100 off), nearly matching its lowest price to date. Like the Mini 2, the rugged, palm-sized satellite communicator lets you send texts, share your location, check the weather, and trigger SOS alerts when you’re off the grid, all while offering battery life that can outlast your average smartphone. Unlike the prior version, though, it features a color touchscreen, which makes it easier to navigate menus and bang out messages. * Garmin’s InReach Messenger Plus is also on sale at REI, Amazon, and direct from Garmin for $299.99 ($100 off), matching its best price to date. The subscription-based Plus model provides satellite connectivity and access to emergency services like the aforementioned InReach Mini 3, except it can also send photos and audio clips in addition to standard text messages. * The Chapter MIPS Bike Helmet is on sale starting at around $112.39 ($41 off) at REI, which nearly matches its best price to date. The lightweight helmet features a hidden PopLock for securing it with a U-lock or chain. It also has a sleek visor and a Micro-USB taillight with 30 lumens of brightness, one that automatically turns on when magnetically attached to the helmet. * Garmin’s Varia RTL515 Radar Taillight is on sale at REI and Amazon for $149.99 ($50 off), which is about $10 less than its all-time low. The headlight combines a bright LED light with a rearview radar that, when paired with a compatible device, warns you of cars approaching from behind from up to 153 yards away. [Product: BCA Tracker 3 Plus Avalanche Transceiver | Camping and travel gear [Product: Exped MegaMat Duo | * A small chair is nice to have for lounging by the campfire, and REI’s Flexlite Camp Chair is a great option now that it’s down to around $67.39 (about $22 off) in multiple colors at REI. It features an aluminum frame, a stable four-leg design, and a ripstop polyester seat with water and stain resistance. When you’re done, it also folds down quickly into a drawstring bag, so you can throw it in your car. [Product: Kelty Low Loveseat | * REI is currently selling its Magma 30 Sleeping Bag in a variety of sizes starting at $243.93 ($105 off). The bag uses 850-fill-power, water-resistant down for warmth and weighs under 20 ounces, depending on the size, making it a great budget pick if you’re looking to get into ultralight backpacking. It also includes a hood to help retain heat, extra room around the feet, and a terrific zipper design that’s less likely to snag when you’re crawling in or out. [Product: REI Siesta Hooded 20 Sleeping Bag | [Product: Rumpl Original Puffy Blanket | * Osprey’s Atmos AG 65 Pack is on sale in several colors and size configurations for around $258.93 ($112 off) at REI, which is one of the lowest prices we’ve seen. The 65-liter pack — which remains a go-to option for The Verge’s own Brandon Widder — is loaded with all sorts of bells and whistles, including an integrated rain cover, a floating top lid, and plenty of compression straps. The hallmark, though, is the ventilation system, which leverages a 3D-suspended mesh for comfort and breathability, making it a great pick for multi-day trips. * REI’s Ruckpack Waist Pack is on sale for $33.69 ($12 off) at REI, which is one of the best prices we’ve seen as of late. Made from a water-repellent material, this small adjustable bag can be worn around your waist or across your body and features three interior pockets for keeping your essentials organized. [Product: Sea to Summit Hanging Toiletry Bag | * The JetBoil Stash Cooking System is a compact, lightweight cooking system that’s currently down to $123.69 (about $41 off) at REI, which is one of the lowest prices we’ve seen all year. It features a standalone stove with a titanium burner and a 0.8-liter cooking pot, allowing you to boil water or heat food at your campsite. The pot comes with a lid and a pour handle, too, and everything can be stowed inside the pot when you’re finished, making it exceptionally easy to pack up. [Product: Sea to Summit Aeros Premium Pillow | * You can buy the ultralight Nemo Tensor in multiple sizes starting at REI for $131.93 (about $88 off). Designed for backpacking, the four-season sleeping pad offers 3.5 inches of cushioning and insulation to keep you warm in colder conditions, with a 5.4 R-value. The nylon construction is also relatively quiet, which, frankly, isn’t the case with many of the camping pads we’ve used over the years. * Nemo’s Stargaze Evo-X is on sale for $99.99 ($80 off) at REI, which is a great price for the surprisingly portable camping chair. The plush, versatile chair automatically reclines when you lean back, making it ideal for relaxing around the campsite (and stargazing). It also features a padded headrest, two cupholders, and a folding frame. And did we mention it swings? Because it swings. * REI’s Wonderland Cot is down to $187.39 ($62 off) at REI. The foldable cot — which is designed more for car camping than anything else — features a spacious, padded sleeping surface, an adjustable backrest, and a sturdy aluminum and steel frame that supports up to 300 pounds. articles.title: Playback singer Rimi Tomy ties the knot with fitness coach Libin Mathew in an intimate wedding
articles.summary: Playback singer and television personality Rimi Tomy has entered a new chapter in her personal life by marrying Libin Mathew, a Malayali bodybuilder and
articles.body: Playback singer and television personality Rimi Tomy has entered a new chapter in her personal life by marrying Libin Mathew, a Malayali bodybuilder and fitness coach based in Mumbai. The wedding took place in Dombivli, Mumbai, on November 14, in the presence of close family members and relatives.Rimi had earlier announced her wedding plans through a video on her YouTube channel, where she opened up about her relationship with Libin and the arrangements for their big day. Sharing why they chose Mumbai as the wedding destination, the singer said, "I usually travel to Bombay once or twice a month anyway. But this time, it's different and a little special. I'm going there for my wedding. Libin was born and brought up in Dombivli, Mumbai. That's why we decided to hold the wedding ceremonies there."Speaking about Libin's background, Rimi said, "Although Libin is a Malayali, he grew up in Mumbai. He started speaking Malayalam only after getting to know me."The singer also revealed that the wedding would be an intimate affair with only ten members from her family, including her mother, siblings and their children. Libin's family members and close relatives would make up the rest of the guest list. Rimi also spoke about her mother's initial concerns regarding the wedding and how the family eventually came around to the decision.The wedding comes seven years after Rimi's divorce from businessman Royce Kizhakoodan. The couple married on April 27, 2008, when Rimi was 24. After 11 years of marriage, they filed for divorce by mutual consent in 2019.Rimi made her playback singing debut with the 2002 Malayalam film Meesa Madhavan. Apart from her singing career, she has also established herself as a popular television host and reality show personality.Get the latest TV News, TV Shows and more. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Thoughts and prayers to anyone flying today.
articles.summary: Nearly 15 percent of all flights scheduled to depart the US on Saturday have been canceled following a nationwide ground stop, according to data from aviation analytics firm Cirium as of 8:30AM ET. Out of 22,232 scheduled US departures — already roughly 4,000 fewer than Friday — 3,262 flights are grounded. JetBlue is taking the biggest hit by percentage, with over 40 percent of its departures canceled, while American, Delta, and United have scrapped between 728 and 880 flights each. Another 267 international flights into the US are also canceled.

articles.title: Bari Weiss at CBS News: A year of drama and challenges as she attempts to revamp the Tiffany Network
articles.summary: Bari Weiss' first year as CBS News editor-in-chief brought newsroom clashes, "60 Minutes" firings and a continuous ratings decline of its newscasts.
articles.body: It has been a tumultuous year for CBS News as the network has been rocked by ownership changes and a polarizing new boss. Last October, then-newly minted Paramount owner David Ellison tapped Bari Weiss as editor-in-chief of CBS News as part of his $150 million purchase of her outlet The Free Press. What has unfolded over the past year is a revolving door of talent, newsroom clashes and a continuous ratings decline. BARI WEISS BEING NAMED TOP CBS NEWS EDITOR CAUSES LIBERAL MEDIA TO MELTDOWN A New Order The battle lines seemed to have been drawn even before Weiss stepped foot inside the CBS newsroom. Her appointment came on the heels of Ellison's $8 billion takeover of Paramount, which critics believe only received the FCC's blessing after Paramount settled President Donald Trump's "60 Minutes" lawsuit for $16 million. Ellison and his billionaire father, Larry Ellison, are perceived as having a cozy relationship with Trump, fueling fear among liberals that he would turn CBS News into MAGA TV. Weiss, who launched The Free Press following her dramatic exit from The New York Times, had been branded by her critics as an anti-woke conservative despite having more heterodox views. When she was appointed by Ellison, she quickly embraced his mission to appeal to the "70%" in the political center rather than the fringes on the left and right. Still, that hasn't stopped outlets such as the left-wing blog The Daily Beast from branding the new CBS chief as being "MAGA-coded." Newsroom clashes Weiss has been a very hands-on editor according to multiple leaked reports, some of which spiraled into contentious newsroom battles. Her first big clash came last December with Sharyn Alfonsi, then a "60 Minutes" correspondent who was set to air a report on the notorious El Salvador prison CECOT but was temporarily shelved at the last minute by Weiss. Weiss insisted at the time that the report wasn't ready and that it needed a voice from the Trump administration, while Alfonsi accused her of playing politics. Liberal critics attacked Weiss, alleging she was trying to censor a report critical of Trump. The segment ultimately aired in January. BARI WEISS FACED 'SIGNIFICANT RESISTANCE' FROM CBS NEWS STAFFERS ABOUT ALASKA BALLOT SCANDAL, INSIDERS SAY Last month, Status reported that Weiss had clashed with veteran correspondent Lesley Stahl during the editing process of a "60 Minutes" segment about Israeli settler violence in the West Bank. The dispute allegedly became so heated that Stahl "privately floated" quitting. A CBS spokesperson called the report "ludicrous." According to Semafor, two CBS News staffers were reportedly upset when Weiss urged journalists to investigate the Democratic Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed's alleged family ties to the Muslim Brotherhood when the controversy erupted. Additionally, a leaked recording from a meeting captured CBS News correspondent Holly Williams having a heated exchange with Weiss' hand-picked foreign editor Shayndi Raice over the network's coverage of Israel and the Oct. 7 terrorist attack, with Raice invoking "legal grounds for firing" and "insubordination" if staff didn't fall in line with the top brass. Anonymous CBS News employees have frequently aired complaints about Weiss to media reporters during her tenure. CBS BOSS FUELS LEFT-WING UPROAR AMID REPORT SHE URGED STAFF TO PROBE ALLEGED EL-SAYED, MUSLIM BROTHERHOOD TIES The "60 Minutes" overhaul Perhaps the most affected CBS News program under Weiss has been "60 Minutes." In May, the network shocked the media landscape when it announced several firings, including "60 Minutes" executive producer Tanya Simon and correspondents Sharyn Alfonsi and Cecilia Vega. Weiss also tapped documentary filmmaker and former New York Times columnist Nick Bilton to replace Simon as the show's top producer. CBS NEWS FIRES '60 MINUTES' CORRESPONDENTS, TOP PRODUCER IN SWEEPING SHAKEUP OF STORIED PROGRAM Tensions further escalated when veteran correspondent Scott Pelley lashed out against Bilton and Weiss at an all-staff meeting days later, where he accused Weiss of "murdering" the storied newsmagazine program and bluntly told Bilton, who has no linear television experience, that he had "slender qualifications" for his new role. That led to Pelley's own termination. With the exit of Anderson Cooper in February, "60 Minutes" suddenly lost four of its seven correspondents. SCOTT PELLEY FIRED AT CBS NEWS AFTER BLOWUPS WITH BARI WEISS, NEW '60 MINUTES' PRODUCER Weiss and Bilton announced in July that they had poached New York Times columnist Ross Douthat and tapped CBS veteran Norah O'Donnell as new "60 Minutes" correspondents, along with several contributors who would join Lesley Stahl, Bill Whitaker and Jon Wertheim. Despite all the reported drama, the new season of "60 Minutes" has closely resembled the program viewers have been used to, except for minor cosmetic changes to graphics and the new personalities leading the reports. And while the show nabbed big exclusives — including interviews with the Air Force service member who was rescued out of Iran earlier this year and the ex-husband of Lindsay Clancy — it didn't result in any major ratings bump as trend lines continue to be unfavorable to "60 Minutes." BARI WEISS POACHES CONSERVATIVE NY TIMES COLUMNIST, OTHERS JOIN '60 MINUTES' IN CBS PROGRAM SHAKEUP The Revolving Door "60 Minutes" isn't the only program to have undergone personnel changes. "CBS Evening News" co-anchors John Dickerson and Maurice DuBois exited the network after just a year at the desk. Weiss handpicked the "CBS Mornings" co-host Tony Dokoupil to lead the evening newscast. His debut was a bit bumpy between being marred by technical difficulties and raised eyebrows for his lighthearted "salute" to Secretary of State Marco Rubio. One of his top producers was also dismissed just days into the show's reboot. Filling Dokoupil's seat alongside Gayle King and Nate Burleson on "CBS Mornings" is Norah O'Donnell, who previously co-hosted what was then called "CBS This Morning" from 2012 to 2019. Weiss also poached Matt Gutman from ABC News as a top correspondent for the network while CBS News reporter Scott MacFarlane headed for the exit. NORAH O'DONNELL URGES LIBERAL BARI WEISS CRITICS TO GIVE 'CBS MORNINGS' A CHANCE AS SHE RETURNS TO PROGRAM The Third Place Struggle For decades, CBS News has been the perpetual third-place broadcaster behind its rivals ABC and NBC. So it was a Herculean task for Weiss to turn things around, especially in just one year. "CBS Mornings" is on pace to have its worst year ever, down to an average of 1.7 million viewers — a 12% drop from last year. That's far below the average 2.9 million and 2.8 million that tune in to "Today" and "Good Morning America" respectively. "CBS Evening News" similarly came in a distant third with its 4 million average viewers, less than half of the 8.3 million who watch "World News Tonight with David Muir" and well behind 6.5 million viewers who watch "NBC Nightly News w/ Tom Llamas." The program did, however, close October with a 16% bump from October 2025. The Tiffany Network's strongest performer, at least in direct competition with its rivals, is its marquee Sunday show "Face the Nation," maintaining its modest lead with 2.9 million average viewers, while ABC's "This Week" and NBC's "Meet The Press" average 2.69 million and 2.5 million respectively, though "Meet The Press" does lead among viewers in the advertiser-coveted demo ages 25-54 while "Face The Nation is second in that metric. "60 Minutes," meanwhile, had its lowest-rated October performance since at least 2000, despite remaining CBS News’ most-watched show. CLICK HERE FOR THE LATEST MEDIA AND CULTURE NEWS Weiss has had a challenging first year, and year two may have its own challenges as Paramount's parent company, Skydance, begins integrating all the properties from its $111 billion purchase of Warner Bros. Discovery, which includes CNN. Rumors of Ellison elevating Weiss to a role overseeing both CBS News and CNN have been put on ice for now. Industry critics remain speculative as to what Ellison has in store for his two news operations as he explores ways to cut costs throughout the company. A spokesperson for CBS News declined to comment. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Fox News' Brian Flood contributed to this report.

articles.title: Got an iPhone Duo? These 9 settings make it easier to use | TechCrunch
articles.summary: From Touch ID shortcuts to smarter volume buttons and camera tricks, these tweaks make Apple's foldable iPhone easier to use every day.
articles.body:
Apple’s new foldable , the iPhone Duo, has proven popular enough that the company can’t keep the device in stock . While the Duo introduces a new way to use an iPhone, getting the most out of this initial version may require adjusting a few settings to make it work better when it comes to everyday tasks, like unlocking the device with Touch ID, navigating the interface, and taking photos.

After spending some time with the Duo, we’d recommend making the following adjustments to make the new iPhone a bit easier to use, most notably when it comes to the use of Touch ID.

Settings to make it easier to live with Touch ID

Unlike modern iPhones, the Duo doesn’t support Face ID. That means you have to adjust to pressing a finger on the side of the device once again to authenticate with apps, unlock the device, and use Apple Pay. But there are a few things you can do to make the switch back to the older technology a bit less painful.

Register extra fingerprints: This may seem like an obvious suggestion, but if you’re used to just registering a fingerprint or two with Touch ID, prepare to rethink that strategy with the Duo. Because the device can be held in multiple orientations, flipped both horizontally and vertically, and because of the small size of the Duo’s screen, you may find that a lot of your fingers (and thumbs!) can now reach the Touch ID button. We’d recommend holding the device in your hand and turning it in different ways, then register the fingerprints where you end up holding the device the most — on both hands. Yes, setting up Touch ID can be a bit tedious compared with Face ID, as there are multiple prints to register. Still, it’s a one-time setup, and later on you’ll be glad that you took the time to make more of your fingerprints work. To register a fingerprint, go to Settings > Touch ID & Passcode > Add a Fingerprint.

Unlock with Apple Watch: If you’re in the market for the iPhone Duo, there’s a good likelihood that you own other Apple devices, like the Apple Watch. If that’s the case, you’re in luck because you can use your Watch to unlock the Duo without having to bother with Touch ID. This will save you time and frustration in the long run, so get used to wearing your Apple Watch more often, especially when you’re out and about and don’t want to fiddle as much with finger placement. To use the Apple Watch unlock, your watch will need to be passcode-protected and worn near your phone. To turn this feature on, go to Settings > Touch ID & Passcode > Unlock with Apple Watch.

Rest finger to Open : This is an optional setting, not necessarily a “must” like the above, but we’ve found it useful. The “rest finger” setting is actually an accessibility feature, but it can double as a usability feature, too. When enabled, you only have to rest your finger lightly on the Touch ID sensor to unlock the device, instead of having to press down. Those who prefer this setting find it can make unlocking the phone faster and more convenient, but others may disagree, as they like the more tactile sensation of a button press. Try it both ways and see which one fits you best. To enable this one, go to Settings > Touch ID & Passcode > Rest Finger to Open .

There are a few settings that could also improve your experience with the iPhone Duo, as they may make it easier to perform certain everyday tasks, like taking screenshots or reaching different parts of the screen, among other things.

Turn off Fixed Volume Controls : This is a favorite hack for new Duo owners, as it makes using the device in any orientation much easier. By default, the iPhone Duo’s volume buttons are “fixed,” which means that no matter how you rotate the device, the Volume Up button remains the button that increases the volume and the Volume Down button decreases it. But many people find it’s easier if the buttons’ functionality rotates with the device. That is, the buttons re-orient themselves based on how you are holding the phone, making the “up” option always on the top or right. As you fold, unfold, and flip the phone, having buttons that flip with you actually makes more sense. To turn off the fixed volume controls, go to Settings > Sounds & Haptics > Fixed Position Volume Controls .

Back Tap for Screenshots : The Duo tries to make it easier to take a screenshot by pressing the side button and either the Volume Up or Volume Down button at the same time. However, you still might find the process a two-handed affair (unless you just ask Siri to do it for you). That’s why many Duo owners are turning to a buried Accessibility feature to make taking screenshots a bit less complicated. In the phone’s accessibility settings, you can configure whether a double tap or triple tap on the back of the device triggers a particular action — which you can set to ‘take a screenshot.’ (Some people prefer the triple tap so they don’t accidentally trigger the feature.) Once enabled, you could hold your Duo in one hand, then use a finger to tap on the back of the phone to take the screenshot, saving you a bit of the hassle that comes with managing the button combinations. To configure this, go to Settings > Accessibility > Touch > Back Tap > then choose a double or triple tap and your action. (Screenshot is under the “Device” menu.)

Reachability : This is another accessibility feature that some Duo owners like to configure, but others like to have off. The option was originally designed to make larger-screened devices easier to use with one hand, which makes it sometimes hard to reach, depending on your hand size. Typically, when Reachability is turned on, the iPhone will lower the top half of the screen to make it easier to reach with your thumb. The Duo does things a little differently, though. Because the phone is wide — it’s shaped like a passport — it’s the far side of the screen that’s harder to reach than the top. So when you turn on Reachability, you will instead be able to swipe the left or right edge of the screen to bring a side into reach. We should note that this feature is enabled by default, but if you find yourself accidentally triggering it and want to turn it off, you can under Settings > Accessibility > Touch > Reachability.

Lock when folded: This one is more of a personal preference, we’ll admit. But if you tend to unfold the device when you’re working with it, then snap it closed when you’re done, you might like to configure a setting that will automatically lock the screen for you when the device is folded shut. However, doing so requires you to create a new shortcut, as there isn’t a setting for this — at least, not yet. To make the shortcut, you’ll open the Shortcuts app, tap the plus (+) sign, then the Edit button in the upper-right. You then tap into the search bar, and tap on the word “ automation ” that appears in blue under the search bar that appears at the top of the screen. Next, you’ll scroll down until you find the option “ Opened or Closed ” under the Display section. Tap that, tap on the word “Opened” to change it to “ Closed ,” then tap in the search bar at the bottom again and type in “ Lock Screen .” Tap on the option “ Lock Screen ” when it appears in the search results, and you’re done — the shortcut has been made. You can tap on the play button here to test it, if you’d like. And if you ever change your mind, just delete the shortcut!

You can tap on the play button here to test it, if you’d like. And if you ever change your mind, just delete the shortcut!

The camera tricks are a little more niche, but some Duo owners have found the following to be helpful.

Customize Camera Controls: The iPhone Duo lets you customize the on-screen layout of the camera controls in the Camera app itself, as part of the latest iOS software update. To use this feature, you’ll open the Camera app and open the six-dot Camera Controls menu in the bottom right. You then tap on the plus sign at the top of the menu (or to the right or left depending on how you’re holding the phone!). This lets you pick and choose which of the camera tools appear above the camera frame itself for quick access, like the flash, or the option to enable or disable Live Photos, or whether Night Mode is on or off, among other things. You can then drag those options to create whichever order makes the most sense for you. (Note: this feature is not exclusive to the Duo.)

Disable Smart Take Flash: The Smart Take feature on the iPhone Duo is designed to help you take hands-free group or solo shots without having to use a self-timer. Instead, you prop up the Duo on a stable surface and activate Smart Take by pressing the button. The camera will detect when there’s movement or the poses change, and the subjects are ready, then takes the picture. But one thing not everyone likes is that each time the photo is captured, the camera flash blinks. This is meant to be a visual clue that lets you know the shot has been taken. However, you can control how the flash behaves during these automatic capture sessions by configuring a setting. To do so, you’ll go to Settings > Camera > Flash During Capture and toggle the switch off if you prefer.
